Iteratively add trees to random forest

Source: R/rf.R
run_iterative_rf.Rd

Trees are added until predictions stabilise or a maximum number of trees is reached.

Usage

run_iterative_rf(
  env_df,
  clust_col = "cluster",
  env_names,
  trees_start = 499,
  trees_add = 249,
  trees_max = 9999,
  rf_cores = 1,
  set_min = FALSE,
  stopping_metric = "f_meas",
  stopping_tolerance = 0.005,
  stopping_runs = 3,
  test_data = FALSE,
  do_imp = FALSE,
  keep_rf = FALSE,
  out_file = NULL,
  force_new = FALSE,
  verbose = base::interactive(),
  ...
)

Arguments

env_df

Dataframe with clust_col, site_col and columns env_names.

clust_col

Character. Name of the columns with clusters.

env_names

Character. Name of the environmental variables (e.g. names(stack_list)).

trees_start

Number of trees in first random forest run.

trees_add

Number of trees to add in each subsequent run.

trees_max

Maximum number of trees in the random forest.

rf_cores

Number of cores to use for parallel processing.

set_min

FALSE or numeric. If numeric, classes in clust_col with less than set_min rows will be filtered

stopping_metric

Character. Either "changed_pred" (proportion of predictions that change between runs) or any metric returned by a summary of yardstick::conf_mat()

stopping_tolerance

What proportion change between runs is acceptable?

stopping_runs

How many runs (in a row) need to beat stopping_tolerance?

test_data

Either FALSE to test against the training data, or new data in same format as env_df, against which to calculate metrics.

do_imp

Logical. Passed to importance argument of randomForest::randomForest().

keep_rf

Logical. If true, randomForest object will be included in output. Defaults to FALSE to save memory.

out_file

Optional name (and path) of file to save results

force_new

Logical. If out_file already exists, should that file be loaded (FALSE) or run again (TRUE) from scratch (and written over).

...

Passed (via make_rf_quick()) to randomForest::randomForest().
